outlook.statement: Management committed to face all challenges and exploit available opportunities to take the company to new heights. Continuous efforts resulted in some increase in the textile segment.

Despite near-term headwinds arising from an uncertain global trade environment and competitive pricing pressures, the medium- to long-term outlook for the Indian textile sector remains constructive, supported by domestic demand, favourable policy measures, and global sourcing diversification. The Company intends to strengthen and diversify its customer base, invest selectively in sustainable and efficiency-enhancing technologies, continue to improve cost efficiency and product mix, and reduce debt gradually and strengthen the balance sheet.

orders_or_contracts.statement: Sale/Job-Work transactions with Shyam Tex Exports Limited approved for aggregate value up to ₹ 60 crore during FY 2026-27

risks: Export growth constrained by soft demand in Europe and US
Intensifying competition from lower-cost manufacturing bases
Related party transactions constitute material portion of business (59.40% of annual consolidated turnover)
Global Economic Risks: A slowdown in key export markets, particularly Europe and the US, may continue to dampen export demand and realisations.

Tariff & Trade Uncertainty: Unpredictable trade policy and rising protectionist measures, including possible tariff hikes in the United States, pose a direct risk to Indian textile exports and to margins and sourcing preferences.
Margin Pressure: Rising wage bills and aggressive pricing from competing manufacturing bases such as Bangladesh and Vietnam continue to compress margins.
Raw Material & Energy Volatility: Cotton prices, along with power and fuel costs, remain volatile and can materially affect input costs.
Liquidity & Working Capital: A tight credit environment and delayed customer payments continue to strain working capital and cash flows.

The Company remains exposed to raw-material price volatility, foreign-exchange fluctuations on account of its export exposure, evolving global trade and tariff policies, and competitive pricing pressures. Working-capital management, particularly the timely realisation of trade receivables in a tight credit environment, continues to be an area of focused attention.
Management of the Company is well aware of risks associated with its business operations and various projects under execution.
